review.summary: The evaluated collagen scaffold model calculates constrained axial stiffness (C_iiii) under a strict kinematic affine strain assumption without solving nodal equilibrium. While scale invariance and symmetry checks pass, the model neglects boundary strut clipping (causing cell-count-dependent density and stiffness inflation), nodal junction volume overlaps, non-affine relaxation, and strut bending/buckling. Its within-model comparisons are valid strictly as upper-bound kinematic orientation metrics for highly constrained systems, provided strut modulus calibration is independently obtained.

findings.title: Unclipped Boundary Struts Cause Size-Dependent Density and Stiffness Inflation
findings.evidence: Strut length sum includes full unclipped outer boundary cylinders while dividing by box volume V = (n * pitch)^3.
findings.implication: Scaffold stiffness C_iiii and nominal solid fraction depend strongly on finite cell count n (e.g. cubic stiffness scales as (n+1)^2 / n^2), overestimating infinite bulk metamaterial properties for small lattice grids.
findings.recommended_check: Evaluate stiffness across n = 1, 3, and 10 to quantify boundary material inflation, and apply boundary strut half-weighting or spatial clipping.

findings.title: Risk of Calibration Circularity if Fitting Strut Modulus to Bulk Compression Data
findings.evidence: Document highlights that back-calculating strut modulus from scaffold stiffness creates circular validation.
findings.implication: Because the affine model overpredicts stiffness by ignoring non-affine relaxation and bending, back-fitting single-strut modulus to bulk experimental data produces an artificially depressed strut modulus.
findings.recommended_check: Enforce input requirements that strut modulus originate from direct single-fibril or single-strut hydrated micro-tensile measurements.

findings.title: Junction Overlap Neglect Overestimates Density at Higher Solid Fractions
findings.evidence: Nominal density is computed as total cylinder volume area * totalLength / V without subtracting vertex intersections.
findings.implication: At larger strut radii, overlapping volume at nodal junctions double-counts material, underestimating true porosity and distorting matched-density comparisons across topologies with different coordination numbers.
findings.recommended_check: Compare nominal line-cylinder density against exact volumetric boolean union (CSG) for strut radius/pitch ratios r/a > 0.05.

findings.title: Affine Kinematic Constraint Distorts Bending vs Stretch Topology Comparisons
findings.evidence: Stiffness uses an affine projection sum sum(A L n_i^4) assuming zero transverse nodal relaxation and pure axial strut strain.
findings.implication: Topologies that deform primarily by bending (e.g., BCC under axial compression) are artificially constrained, overstating their relative stiffness compared to stretch-dominated lattices (e.g., octet/cubic).
findings.recommended_check: Compare affine stiffness ratios E_octet / E_bcc against elastic frame or beam finite element calculations with free internal nodal equilibrium.

findings.title: Scale Invariance Preserved Under Isotropic Pitch and Radius Rescaling
findings.evidence: Proportional scaling of cell pitch and strut radius maintains solid fraction and affine stiffness C_iiii.
findings.implication: The linear axial-strut kinematic formulation correctly obeys standard continuum scale invariance when geometric proportions remain constant.
findings.recommended_check: Verify scale invariance test in test-model.js line 13 when scaling pitch and radius simultaneously.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: Under complete kinematic affine constraint (such as high lateral confinement or rigid matrix embedding), the model's stiffness metrics accurately rank lattices according to the axial projection factor sum(A L n_z^4) / V at equal nominal line-volume fractions.
review.decisive_next_experiment: Perform unconfined compression testing on 3D-fabricated micro-lattice scaffolds combined with optical Digital Image Correlation (DIC) to measure non-affine nodal displacements and local strut bending/buckling, using independently measured single-strut hydrated modulus (via micro-tensile testing) as input.

literature_to_verify.query: octet truss lattice non-affine displacement relaxation stiffness reduction
literature_to_verify.reason: Quantify the departure of actual relaxed lattice stiffness from the unrelaxed affine kinematic upper bound.

literature_to_verify.query: collagen single fibril hydrated tensile modulus micro-tensile nanoindentation
literature_to_verify.reason: Obtain non-circular, independently measured hydrated strut modulus values for calibration input.
